items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Well gosh, you have a pretty good list of well known names you’ve played with. Milt Hinton and Bob Wilber and all those guys. Was most of that at festivals?

ctx.x: And he plays closed rolls and the hi-hat. Yeah. I remember him doing that. And a stick on the bass drum. That’s a technique you don’t see too much anymore. Keep a four beat going on the bass drum and play a little syncopation against it with either the left or the right stick. I’d do that this weekend but with that 18-inch bass drum I’ll drop a stick reaching for it.
Well gosh, you have a pretty good list of well known names you’ve played with. Milt Hinton and Bob Wilber and all those guys. Was most of that at festivals?

Mostly things like this, like jazz party work and mix and match. There’ll be one person hiring everybody who’ll put together a set of musicians he thinks will work well together; 99% of the time they do. But that’s where I’ve gotten to work with really great players like that. Because you know they travel in their own circles. And if they’re going to need a drummer, they’re going to call someone they’re comfortable with who they work with all the time. But that’s the great advantage for me having played these…
